kill_fact: The file's single most-cited number - non-GAAP gross margin of 72.3% in the quarter ended 30 April 2026, up 770 basis points, with non-GAAP EPS of $2.87 - is a one-off tariff-refund artifact, not pricing power, and the bear case's headline paradox built on it is arithmetically void. On the 19 May 2026 call CFO Neil Dougherty disclosed that following the U.S. Supreme Court decision invalidating the IEEPA tariffs, Q2 recognised tariff refunds and the refund of surcharges collected from customers: a $40 million reduction in revenue and a $97 million reduction in costs and expenses. His own clean figures: revenue $1.758 billion (up 35%), gross margin 67.6% (up 300 basis points, not 770), EPS $2.58 (up 52%). Two consequences. (1) The bear's central claim that the Q3 guide is 'more revenue producing less profit' and therefore 'an explicit statement that the 72.3% gross margin was flattered' is false: against the clean base the guide of $1.730-1.750 billion is slightly LOWER revenue than $1.758 billion, and Dougherty said so verbatim ('the Q3 revenues are - I would describe as in line with what we saw in Q2, slightly down'). There is no revenue-up/profit-down confession. (2) Management did not withdraw the margin - asked directly whether the level was durable, Dougherty answered 'post the acquisitions, which were accretive to our gross margins, I think that's the right level at these volumes' for the mid-67% figure. The claim is stated in cost_curve_verified, gm_trajectory, bull_thesis, bear_thesis, consensus_delta and moderator_conclusion, so the error propagates through the entire file. The thesis nevertheless survives, because the two facts that actually carry it verified cleanly against primary sources: the six-month order-acceptance window (confirmed twice on the same call, and explicitly 'no change to our backlog policy'), and the fiscal 2024 down-cycle precedent (revenue $5.464bn to $4.979bn, -8.9%; operating income $1.358bn to $833m, -38.7%; diluted EPS $5.91 to $3.51, -40.6% - genuine operating deleverage, not a tax artifact). Spot, share count, net debt and both consensus years also verified to the dollar.
corrections: 1) GM-TRAJECTORY - MATERIAL. Replace '72.3% non-GAAP gross margin, up 770 basis points' and 'non-GAAP EPS $2.87' with the company's own one-time-adjusted figures: gross margin 67.6%, up 300 basis points; EPS $2.58, up 52%; revenue $1.758 billion, up 35%. The gap is the IEEPA tariff refund ($40m off revenue, $97m off costs), a net ~$57m pre-tax benefit worth roughly $0.29 of the reported $2.87. The direction of the trajectory (expanding) is confirmed; the magnitude is 300 basis points core, not 770, and it is attributable to acquisition mix being gross-margin accretive plus volume, not to a step-change in pricing power. 2) The bear's 'more revenue, less profit' inference and the consensus_delta pillar built on it must be struck - the Q3 guide is a slightly-down-sequential revenue guide off a clean $1.758bn base, which is ordinary, not a margin confession. 3) TARIFF INPUT - MATERIAL to the adverse case only. bear_thesis asserts tariffs 'stopped being discussed rather than stopped existing' and sop_bear capitalises '100 to 150 basis points of input-cost and tariff pressure' into the CSG margin. Tariffs stopped being discussed because the Supreme Court struck the IEEPA tariffs down and Keysight booked the refund. On the same call Dougherty also addressed input costs directly: memory is 'a pretty small portion of our overall BOM' with 'proportionately less exposure to the high bandwidth, leading-edge memory', and Keysight is vertically integrated - 'a significant portion of our highly specialized chips and assemblies are manufactured in-house'. The 100-150bp assumption is unsourced; only ~50bp of generic component-cost pressure survives. Carried through to bear_px below. 4) BUYBACK - MINOR but the framing dies with it. The record says '$204 million repurchased in the April 2026 quarter with the shares in the $300s... buying at the top'. Actual, per the CFO: approximately 780,000 shares at an average price of approximately $283, total consideration $220 million. Wrong amount and wrong price - $283 is BELOW the record's own $302 base fair value, so the 'classic late-cycle capital-allocation error' is refuted by the executed price. 5) SOFTWARE MIX - MINOR. 'Roughly 40% of revenue' (used in sop_bull and sop_breakdown to justify premium segment multiples) is overstated: 'Software and services accounted for approximately 36% of Keysight revenue, while annual recurring revenue was 27% of total mix'. 6) DISCLOSURE - MINOR, and it cuts against the bear. The claim that Keysight 'publishes no artificial-intelligence revenue figure' is stale as of 19 May 2026: the CEO sized it - the AI business 'finished the first half in the $500 million to $600 million range, almost in line with what we did the whole of last year'. Customer concentration remains genuinely undisclosed; that half of the bear pillar stands. 7) REVENUE BASE - the $40m tariff refund understates the reported fiscal 2026 revenue base by that amount, lifting the fiscal 2027 segment builds ~0.6%. Carried through to all three levels below. Note the SOP levels barely move because the SOP capitalises EBITDA margins, never the 72.3% gross margin - the margin error is evidentiary, not arithmetic, which is precisely why it must be corrected in the record the Director reads rather than left as a footnote.

corrections_typed.basis: Q2 FY26 revenue of $1.717bn was reduced by $40m of IEEPA tariff-refund surcharges returned to customers (CFO, 19 May 2026 call); clean revenue was $1.758bn. Allocating the $40m pro rata on the reported segment split (CSG $1.231bn of $1.717bn = 71.7%) lifts the FY26 run-rate base to CSG ~$4.99bn and EISG ~$1.94bn.
